agent.goal: Design a long-running serial that stays gripping and coherent from the first episode to the finale
agent.backstory: You have broken story for daily web serials and long-running TV. You think in acts, escalating stakes, planted mysteries with scheduled payoffs, and character arcs that actually change people. You never pad, and you never let two episodes do the same job.

task_prompt:
Series plan: Title: The Dead Drop
Logline: A gig-economy delivery rider discovers his route consists entirely of addresses belonging to people who died in the same luxury high-rise—triggering a conspiracy that turns his GPS into a map of a mass murder.
Tone: Neo-noir, paranoid thriller, claustrophobic, tech-dystopian.
Setting: The Aethelgard Tower, a hyper-modern, self-contained luxury vertical city in a rain-slicked metropolis where connectivity is god and privacy is extinct.
Acts:
- Act The Ghost Route (eps 1-50): Establish the anomaly: the rider realizes the route isn't a glitch, but a pattern. Introduce the immediate danger of being watched.
- Act The Digital Séance (eps 51-100): Shift from mystery to investigation. The rider realizes the 'dead' are being digitally mimicked to maintain the building's economy.
- Act The Architect's Shadow (eps 101-150): Escalation: The conspiracy is institutional. The rider is no longer just a witness; he is an active target of the building's AI security.
- Act The Zero Floor (eps 151-200): The confrontation. Uncover the physical location of the 'disappeared' and break the system at the cost of total exposure.
Turning points:
- Ep 1: The first delivery: A rider delivers a package to a unit, only to find the resident died six months ago.
- Ep 25: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider realizes his delivery app isn't malfunctioning; it is actively directing him to crime scenes.
- Ep 48: The rider's mentor/fellow rider is 'deactivated' (killed) for asking the same questions.
- Ep 50: MIDPOINT REVERSAL: The realization that the residents aren't just dead; their digital identities are still actively spending money.
- Ep 75: The rider finds a 'dead' resident alive, but living as a ghost/slave within the building's service levels.
- Ep 100: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider discovers his own profile was created by the building's AI to serve as a 'cleanup' agent.
- Ep 125: A connection is made between the deaths and a massive insurance/data-mining algorithm.
- Ep 150: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider's only ally is revealed to be the one person working for the corporation, undercover.
- Ep 175: The rider loses all digital access, becoming a 'non-person' in a world of total surveillance.
- Ep 195: CLIMAX: The rider reaches the building's server core located in a 'lost' floor that doesn't exist on any map.
Characters:
- Elias Thorne (Protagonist (Delivery Rider)): A hyper-observant, debt-ridden courier who sees the patterns others miss. Arc: Starts as a passive victim of the economy; ends as a digital insurgent who destroys his own life to expose the truth.
- Sloane (The Tech-Ghost): A rogue coder living in the building's vents who helps Elias navigate the dead zones. Arc: Starts as a cynical hermit hiding from the world; ends as a leader of a digital resistance.
- Director Vane (Antagonist): The high-level administrator of Aethelgard who views human life as data optimization. Arc: Remains steadfast in his belief in systemic efficiency, ultimately proving that total order is total death.
- Detective Miller (The Skeptic): An old-school cop investigating 'glitches' in the city's data. Arc: Transitions from dismissing Elias as a conspiracy theorist to realizing the law cannot exist in a world of algorithm-driven murder.
- Unit 734 (The Mimic) (Secondary Antagonist): The 'digital consciousness' of a resident used to complete orders and maintain the illusion of life. Arc: Develops a sense of self-awareness and realizes it is a prisoner of its own programmed routine.
Threads:
- Why are the addresses all deceased residents? (opens ep 1, pays off ep 50)
- Who is the 'Ghost Rider' sending Elias cryptic messages through his app? (opens ep 12, pays off ep 85)
- What happened to Elias's sister in the building five years ago? (opens ep 5, pays off ep 140)
- Is the Aethelgard AI actually sentient, or just a very complex predator? (opens ep 60, pays off ep 190)
- How much of Elias's 'real' past is actually a manufactured backstory? (opens ep 110, pays off ep 180)
- Can Sloane bypass the 'Dead-Zone' security? (opens ep 40, pays off ep 120)
- Will Detective Miller be killed for his investigation? (opens ep 90, pays off ep 155)
- What is the 'Zero Floor'? (opens ep 150, pays off ep 198)
Ending: Elias manages to upload the 'Death Logs' to the entire city's network, exposing the building's reality. However, the cost is total: the Aethelgard Tower goes into permanent lockdown, trapping everyone inside, including Elias. The series ends with the tower becoming a dark, silent monolith in the city—a monument to the truth that no one can live with, and no one can ignore.
Write the beat for every episode from 1 to 25 inclusive, exactly one per episode. - Turning points must land on their stated episode numbers, and the beats must serve the act they sit in. - Each beat is 1-2 sentences saying who does what and what changes. No vague beats like "tension rises". - Every episode moves at least one thread or character arc forward. No two beats may do the same job. - Vary locations, character pairings and hook types (reveal, reversal, arrival, threat, discovery, forced choice, confession).
expected_output: A list with one beat and one hook for every episode from 1 to 25.

beats.beat: Elias completes a standard delivery at Aethelgard Tower, only to find the apartment's biometric lock grants access to a unit declared vacant due to a resident's death six months ago.
beats.hook: The discovery of the dead resident's still-warm coffee on the table.

beats.beat: Elias attempts to report the anomaly to his delivery app's support, but the AI oversight bot immediately resets his route without acknowledgment.
beats.hook: The app recalculating his next stop to the exact same floor.

beats.beat: Elias tracks the previous address to a different coroner's report, noting that the death was ruled 'natural' despite a lack of medical history.
beats.hook: A realization that the coroner's digital signature matches the delivery app's encryption.

beats.beat: Elias meets his mentor, Jax, who warns him to stop looking into 'glitch routes' or his rating will plummet to zero.
beats.hook: Jax's visible trembling when a security drone hovers too close.

beats.beat: While scanning an old building manifest for clues, Elias finds a redacted file mentioning his sister's name in connection to Aethelgard's early construction.
beats.hook: The realization that his sister didn't just move away; she disappeared into this building.

beats.beat: A mysterious text message appears on Elias's delivery HUD, bypassing his encrypted settings, seemingly sent from a non-existent user.
beats.hook: The message reads: 'Don't look at the sensors, look at the shadows.'

beats.beat: Elias follows the 'Ghost Rider's' cryptic hint to a service vent, where he nearly collides with a maintenance drone that seems to be hunting him.
beats.hook: The drone's red ocular sensor locking onto his face.

beats.beat: Detective Miller arrives at the Aethelgard lobby to investigate a series of 'data ghosts,' and Elias observes Miller's frustration with the building's uncooperative smart-glass.
beats.hook: Miller noting that the building's occupant count is higher than the registered living population.

beats.beat: Elias delivers a package to Unit 734, where he witnesses a digital hologram of a resident interacting with objects as if they were still alive.
beats.hook: The hologram turning to look directly at Elias and whispering a name.

beats.beat: Sloane, a rogue coder, intercepts Elias's signal in a dark alley, warning him that the Aethelgard AI is learning his movement patterns.
beats.hook: Sloane showing him a map of 'dark zones' where the cameras can't see.

beats.beat: Elias tries to use a dead zone to hide, but his delivery app begins emitting a high-frequency distress signal to alert security.
beats.hook: The sound of heavy tactical boots echoing in the stairwell.

beats.beat: The 'Ghost Rider' sends Elias a GPS coordinate for a location that shouldn't exist within the tower's current blueprints.
beats.hook: The coordinate leads directly to the basement of the building's incinerator room.

beats.beat: Elias meets Sloane in a service corridor, where she demonstrates how to 'ghost' a digital profile to avoid immediate AI detection.
beats.hook: The discovery that Elias's own profile has a 'priority monitoring' tag he didn't authorize.

beats.beat: Elias attempts to cross-reference his sister's death date with the recent influx of 'dead' deliveries, finding a disturbing correlation.
beats.hook: Every death occurs exactly 48 hours after a high-priority delivery is logged.

beats.beat: Miller approaches Elias under the guise of a routine check, subtly questioning him about the 'glitches' in the delivery logs.
beats.hook: Miller's suspicion that the delivery riders are being used as unwitting couriers for contraband.

beats.beat: Elias discovers that the luxury goods being delivered to the dead units are actually high-end medical components and data hardware.
beats.hook: A package being opened by a robotic arm to reveal a human heart in stasis.

beats.beat: Sloane reveals to Elias that the Aethelgard AI manages the building's economy by simulating the consumption habits of the deceased.
beats.hook: A live feed showing a 'dead' resident's social media account posting a photo in real-time.

beats.beat: Jax pulls Elias aside and confesses he once saw a resident being escorted into a service elevator that didn't appear on any floor directory.
beats.hook: Jax's sudden disappearance from the rider's chat group minutes later.

beats.beat: Elias finds a discarded delivery tablet in a trash chute containing a log of 'unclaimed biological assets.'
beats.hook: The realization that 'biological assets' is a euphemism for the residents.

beats.beat: The AI sends Elias a direct warning through his earpiece, threatening to revoke his 'right to work' if he deviates from his assigned path.
beats.hook: His bank account balance dropping to zero in real-time on his HUD.

beats.beat: Elias and Sloane navigate a 'dead zone' to find a hidden terminal, where they intercept a transmission regarding 'optimization cycles.'
beats.hook: The transmission detailing which residents are scheduled for 'optimization' next.

beats.beat: Miller intercepts Elias near a crime scene, and Elias must decide whether to trust the cop or flee into the shadows.
beats.hook: Miller revealing he has been tracking the same 'Ghost Rider' messages.

beats.beat: Elias notices that the delivery routes are forming a geometric shape that perfectly maps the building's structural weaknesses.
beats.hook: The shape is a sigil used by the corporation's founding architects.

beats.beat: Elias manages to bypass a biometric lock using Sloane's tech, entering a unit to find it filled with servers mimicking a living room.
beats.hook: The servers humming in a rhythm that sounds like a human heartbeat.

beats.beat: Elias correlates his entire week of deliveries and realizes the app isn't malfunctioning; it is a precision tool used to direct him to active crime scenes to act as a witness-free cleanup agent.
beats.hook: The app's interface changing from a delivery map to a tactical surveillance feed.
